chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has a servant to serve him, and he says, 'She is for so-and-so to serve him for as long as he lives. So when he dies, she is free.' The servant absconds five or six years before the man dies. Then his heirs find her. Is it for them to make her serve in accordance with what she absconded? He said: 'When the man died, she was free.'
ai.seo_question: Do heirs of a master have the right to deduct the years a lifetime servant was absent before his death from her service period?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling of *Mudabbirah* (a slave designated for emancipation upon the owner's death), ruling that her freedom is immediate and unconditional upon the master's death, regardless of any prior period of absence (*i'bq*). This highlights the Shia juristic view that the condition of death is the sole trigger for emancipation, distinguishing it from other forms of servitude where service duration might be calculated. The ruling underscores the generosity inherent in manumission contracts, ensuring the servant is not penalized for absconding before the final event of death.
